lesson_title: Conversions and Estimating: Paint, Ovens and the Second Trip to the Shop
hook_text: The label says 5 litres covers 20 square metres. Your wall is 54. Here's how not to make a second trip.
clip_script: Five litres covers twenty square metres. So one litre covers four. Your wall is fifty-four square metres and it needs two coats — that's a hundred and eight square metres of covering. Divide by four: twenty-seven litres. But here's where school maths stops and real life starts. Nobody sells you twenty-seven litres. The shop has five-litre tins at R429 and a twenty-litre drum at R1 549. One drum plus two tins is thirty litres for R2 407. Six tins is also thirty litres — for R2 574. Same paint. R167 difference. So the answer isn't twenty-seven litres. The answer is: buy the drum and two tins. And while you're in the kitchen — granny's recipe says 350 degrees, but that's Fahrenheit. Take the 32 off FIRST: 318. Times five: 1 590. Divide by nine: 176,67. Set your oven to 180. Take the 32 off first coming down, put it on last going up. Get that order wrong and your cake is a brick.
visual_style: A hardware aisle and a kitchen counter cut together — tins stacking into litres, a wall filling with colour, an oven dial swinging from Fahrenheit numbers to Celsius, price tags flipping to show the R167 gap.
mood: Practical, warm, slightly conspiratorial — insider knowledge about not wasting money.
pacing: Brisk through the paint arithmetic, a beat on the price comparison, deliberate on the temperature steps.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and get every conversion right the first time.
